title: Policy And Standards: From Rule To Institutional Implementation
summary: Follow federal policy into recurring agency control measurement, named FISMA panels, tested systems, incidents, corrective actions, recovery, and mission outcomes.
current_state_summary: NASA, DHS, and HHS now have named multi-year FISMA panels, with annual metric, scope, sampling, and component boundaries kept visible.
current_state: OMB memoranda define federal AI use, acquisition, and covered-LLM control points without proving agency implementation.
GSA's OneGov channel makes selected AI offerings purchasable under stated terms without establishing adoption or outcomes.
NIST's post-quantum standards move the problem into inventory, procurement, product, credential, and migration work.
GSA's PQC buyer's guide maps inventory, planning, implementation, maintenance, training, and use cases to acquisition support and contract vehicles without proving an agency order.
PIV working drafts expose proposed credential changes but remain preliminary rather than final requirements.
O-RAN testbed artifacts and version 1.7 software provide inspectable experimental implementation, not a final 6G standard or commercial deployment.
Annual federal reports can be followed as series only when the covered agency set, metric definition, method, and revision history remain explicit.
NASA remained at Level 3 across FY 2022-FY 2024, DHS moved from ineffective in FY 2021 to effective in FY 2022 and FY 2023, and HHS remained Not Effective across FY 2022-FY 2024.
The three agency sequences remain separate and do not support a cross-agency rank.
Phase 56C adds entity-matched controls, inputs, constraints, later observations, attribution, independent-validation limits, and alternative explanations.
Temporal order is preserved without converting association into causation, ranking, composite scoring, or readiness scoring.
Phase 56D adds later observations and explicit tests of named Phase 56C alternative explanations for the same twelve entities.
Compatibility, attribution, validation status, missing denominators, and series breaks remain visible before any interpretation.
Phase 56E adds a second vertically replicated cohort: Department of Veterans Affairs, Department of Energy, Department of Transportation.
Every retained entity carries a panel, a driver-and-constraint dossier, and an alternative-explanation test under one stable identity.
Phase 56F assigns every entity one highest-value missing record, one strongest compatible current record, a closure state, and an explicit reopening rule.
Across all 24 entities, one bounded record is Closed, sixteen are Partially Closed, and seven remain Open; these are evidence states, not performance measures.
Phase 56G checked 2 exact record rails in this pathway and retained the Phase 56F reopening rules.
The selected exact records remain Open; current adjacent records are preserved as dated checks rather than closures.
Phase 56H checked 6 named records in this pathway against existing coverage IDs and continuation rules.
1 selected evidence state advances from Open to Partially Closed; the remaining denominators stay explicit.
Phase 56I completes 1 first-pass decision in this pathway while retaining each coverage ID and continuation rule.
No selected closure state changes; genuinely new denominators publish and repeated evidence remains referenced rather than relabeled as a new finding.
Phase 56J adds 1 named continuation decision to this pathway under the ordered evidence-value queue.
Acquisition order describes evidence opportunity and does not rank entities, performance, safety, quality, readiness, or value.
Phase 56K checks 3 exact named records in this pathway and preserves explicit non-closures.
An exact-record check can improve the evidence rail without changing the selected closure state.
Phase 56M adds an exact sixteen-action NASA non-closure and two bounded HHS provider control tests.
Open, implemented, closed, tested-effective, and no-recommendation states remain distinct.
Phase 56N adds nine exact federal remediation or component outcomes and one held dated HHS check.
Closed-Implemented, Open, Open-Partially Addressed, no-longer-valid, component, portfolio, and held states remain distinct.
Phase 56O adds seven exact agency priority portfolios and one bounded government-wide potential-benefit model.
Implemented, added, de-prioritized, current, modeled, and realized states remain distinct.
Phase 56P decomposes four federal priority portfolios into twenty-two stable letter-named actions without inventing recommendation numbers or implementation states.

dependency_stack.current_state: OMB memoranda define agency governance, acquisition, evaluation, privacy, data-rights, interoperability, and risk requirements.
dependency_stack.boundary: A memorandum does not prove that an agency has inventoried systems, changed contracts, trained staff, implemented controls, or measured results.

dependency_stack.current_state: GSA OneGov provides a current path for eligible agencies to buy selected AI offerings under negotiated terms.
dependency_stack.boundary: Availability and promotional pricing do not establish orders, authorization, integration, usage, productivity, renewal cost, or mission outcome.

dependency_stack.current_state: NIST post-quantum standards establish algorithms that organizations can begin to implement.
dependency_stack.boundary: Standards availability is not a cryptographic inventory, validated product, contract change, deployment, or completed migration.

dependency_stack.current_state: GSA's buyer's guide identifies acquisition steps, implementation work, use cases, support, and contract vehicles for federal agencies.
dependency_stack.boundary: Guidance and available vehicles do not prove an agency inventory, solicitation, order, validation, pilot, deployment, or retirement.

dependency_stack.current_state: PIV working drafts make proposed credential, certificate, and interface changes visible.
dependency_stack.boundary: NIST labels the materials preliminary; they are not final requirements or deployed federal capability.

dependency_stack.current_state: NIST records accepted O-RAN artifacts and a documented version 1.7 experimental automation release.
dependency_stack.boundary: Laboratory artifacts do not prove broad interoperability, certification, security assurance, a final standard, or commercial service.

dependency_stack.current_state: Recurring federal reporting now supplies multiple observations beyond one policy or one audit.
dependency_stack.boundary: Reporting continuity is not equivalent to implementation effectiveness or operating benefit.

dependency_stack.current_state: Nine inspector-general records support three stable agency-level control panels.
dependency_stack.boundary: Agency maturity and effectiveness labels do not share identical scope, sampling, metric design, system risk, incident exposure, or mission consequence.

dependency_stack.current_state: Twelve dossiers order baseline, intervention or input, constraint, and later observation.
dependency_stack.boundary: Temporal sequence and attribution do not establish causal effect.

dependency_stack.current_state: Twelve entity tests map later records to named competing explanations.
dependency_stack.boundary: A test may narrow an explanation without isolating cause or producing a score.

dependency_stack.current_state: Twelve additional entities passed a four-primary-record screen and received all three evidence layers.
dependency_stack.boundary: Entity depth can increase without making different entities comparable.

dependency_stack.current_state: One selected record and one reopening rule now govern each of the 24 named entities.
dependency_stack.boundary: Closed, Partially Closed, and Open describe the selected evidence question only; they do not compare entity performance.

dependency_stack.current_state: The exact records remain Open after current named-source checks.
dependency_stack.boundary: A current source is not a closure unless it supplies the selected record, compatible denominator, attribution, and observation window.

dependency_stack.current_state: Compatible bounded records advance selected evidence states while full operating and outcome denominators remain open.
dependency_stack.boundary: Evidence movement is not entity performance; adjacent context cannot replace a missing annual, monthly, interval, closure, restoration, or outcome denominator.

dependency_stack.current_state: Every remaining Open and Partially Closed queue item has a dated decision; two genuinely new bounded denominators publish.
dependency_stack.boundary: A first-pass decision, monthly record, program commitment, or current source check is not full closure or entity performance.

dependency_stack.current_state: Five named records are reviewed; four bounded findings publish, one scope mismatch remains held, and only Manatee changes evidence state.
dependency_stack.boundary: A monthly row, constraint entry, operator event, official plan, or component audit is not complete performance or a causal result.

dependency_stack.current_state: Seven named records are checked; three bounded observations publish, four exact non-closures are recorded, and no evidence state changes.
dependency_stack.boundary: A response filing, recommendation icon, arrival date, index check, audit catalog, fleet report, or audit initiation is not a differently scoped final result.

dependency_stack.current_state: NASA has sixteen exact open GAO actions; two anonymous HHS provider tests publish with distinct findings, scopes, and periods.
dependency_stack.boundary: Selected provider tests do not establish department or sector performance, and open status does not establish severity or operational failure.

dependency_stack.stage: Phase 56N verified remediation and component outcomes
dependency_stack.current_state: Six agency AI-governance rails, a DHS priority portfolio, DOE insider-threat remediation, and a VA component follow-up now have exact current recommendation states.
dependency_stack.boundary: Recommendation states, portfolio movement, and component closures do not establish system performance, enterprise effectiveness, service outcomes, or readiness.

dependency_stack.current_state: Seven agency portfolios now expose annual implementation throughput, additions, designation changes, and current workload; GAO also supplies a bounded government-wide benefit model.
dependency_stack.boundary: Portfolio arithmetic and modeled potential benefit do not establish agency performance, realized savings, safety, quality, readiness, or causation.

dependency_stack.current_state: Phase 56P decomposes four federal priority portfolios into twenty-two stable letter-named actions without inventing recommendation numbers or implementation states.
dependency_stack.boundary: A local action key and open priority designation do not establish a GAO database identity, implementation, closure, operating outcome, or agency performance.

evidence_limits: The pathway does not establish which agencies have implemented the OMB AI controls or purchased, integrated, and evaluated OneGov offerings.

The post-quantum record now has a procurement path but still lacks institution-level inventories, orders, product validation, vendor readiness, budget, staffing, pilot, deployment, and retirement evidence.
Preliminary PIV working drafts can change and should not be described as final requirements.
NIST O-RAN laboratory evidence does not stand in for spectrum decisions, industry consensus, certification, secure deployment, or commercial adoption.
Administrative reporting can change scope, metric design, maturity scale, automation, and publication location.
Annual FISMA metrics, tested systems, evaluator scope, component coverage, and calculated-rating methods can change.
An agency-level rating does not establish system-level control operation, incident reduction, service continuity, or mission benefit.
A named intervention, control, input, or response does not by itself explain an observed outcome.
Company and operator claims remain attributed until independently validated.
A recommendation status, certification, supplier clause, incident response, monthly cause mix, or complaint count does not create a common performance measure.
Different units, methods, identities, observation windows, and attribution levels remain split.
The second cohort preserves attribution, unit, denominator, method, observation window, reporting breaks, and identity changes.
A vertical entity record does not authorize cross-entity ranking, composite scoring, readiness scoring, or causal inference.
Phase 56F closure states apply to one named missing record per entity and cannot be converted into a ranking, composite, readiness score, or causal claim.
Phase 56G acquisition outcomes measure evidence closure only and cannot be converted into entity performance, a comparison, or a score.
Phase 56H closure and deepening states cannot be converted into rankings, scores, readiness, quality, safety, value, or causal claims.
Phase 56I first-pass and closure states cannot be converted into rankings, scores, readiness, quality, safety, value, or causal claims.
Phase 56J acquisition order and closure states cannot be converted into rankings, scores, readiness, quality, safety, value, or causal claims.
Phase 56K exact-record decisions cannot be converted into rankings, scores, readiness, quality, safety, value, or causal claims.
Phase 56M records cannot be converted into agency or provider rankings, readiness scores, value scores, or causal claims.
Phase 56N records cannot be converted into agency or provider rankings, readiness scores, value scores, performance rates, or causal claims.
The HHS post-July 29 check remains held because a passed expected-update date is not a remediation result or formal missed-deadline finding.
Phase 56O portfolio counts use different agency inventories and subject mixes and cannot support agency rankings or comparable rates.
The $132 billion to $251 billion range is modeled potential benefit, not a forecast, appropriation, agency allocation, or realized saving.
A local action key and open priority designation do not establish a GAO database identity, implementation, closure, operating outcome, or agency performance.
FTFN Phase 56P action keys are stable local references, not official GAO Recommendations Database numbers.
